name: Casco Historico
tagline: Granite old town around the cathedral
description: The UNESCO-listed medieval core, a maze of granite streets, arcades and plazas centred on the great cathedral and the Praza do Obradoiro. Pedestrianised, atmospheric and full of tapas bars, it is the beating heart of pilgrim and tourist life.
bestFor: Culture lovers wanting history, walkability and cafes on the doorstep
pros: Bars, markets and sights on the doorstep
cons: Wifi patchy in old stone buildings

name: Ensanche
tagline: Modern new town by Praza de Galicia
description: The nineteenth and twentieth-century new town spreading south from Praza de Galicia, with wider streets, shops, offices and most of the city's coworking spaces. Practical and well connected, it offers modern flats and reliable fibre a short walk from the old town.
bestFor: Remote workers wanting modern flats, coworking and good connectivity
pros: Short walk to the old town

name: Vista Alegre
tagline: Leafy student area near the university
description: A residential district close to the university campuses, popular with students and young residents. Quieter and greener than the centre, it mixes affordable flats with parks and everyday cafes, giving a relaxed, studious feel within easy walking distance of the old town.
bestFor: Budget-minded nomads wanting a calm, youthful residential base
pros: Close to campus cafes and parks

name: Fontinas
description: A practical residential neighbourhood on the north-eastern edge of the city, near the shopping area and bus links. It offers some of the best-value flats in Santiago, a local, non-touristy atmosphere and easy access to supermarkets and services for longer stays.
bestFor: Long-stay nomads prioritising space, value and local everyday living
cons: Longer walk to the old town
